w10_P4_003160: At a materials lab a pneumatic sled with a mass of 21000 g rests on a level track. The launch controller reads the two dial settings 2 and 6, adds them together, and multiplies the sum by 8 to fix the release speed of the sled in metres per second. When the sled is released the logger records the energy the sled carries because of its motion, and prints that figure in kilojoules. Immediately afterwards three booster capacitors discharge into the same running total, adding 19 kJ, then 18 kJ, then 10 kJ. What does the running total read once the third capacitor has fired, in kJ?
w10_P4_003168: A packing line has one hopper holding 111 bolts and another holding 211 washers. The supervisor picks the largest crate capacity, in items, that would empty either hopper into completely full crates with nothing left over, and the maintenance team then adds 22 to that number to set the release speed, in metres per second, of a test carriage on the neighbouring rig. The carriage has a mass of 8000 g and runs on a level rail, and the bench it stands on is 1.4 m long. The logger records the energy the moving carriage carries, the run is repeated until 9 identical carriages have been launched, and the combined figure is written down in kilojoules. That kilojoule figure is then multiplied by 5 to give the total charged to the shift. What is the shift total, in kJ?
w10_P4_003169: A calibration curve on a lab bench gives the stored charge as 3 times the cube of the dial reading, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the dial reading. The technician needs to know how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at a dial reading of 1.0, and that number is entered as the launch speed, in metres per second, of a trolley of mass 12000 g on the adjacent rail. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded in joules. A brake pad removes 4 J from that figure and a spring kick then puts 10 J back. The same procedure is carried out with 3 identical trolleys and the three results are added together. The bench coil has a resistance of 47 ohms. What is the combined figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_003172: A goods lift raises a platform whose mass is 180 kg inside a shaft 12 m tall. The control panel takes the two calibration numbers 4 and 5, adds them, and multiplies the sum by 5 to fix the acceleration of the platform in metres per second squared. The engineer works out the force the motor must apply to the platform to produce that acceleration and expresses it in kilonewtons. The building has 7 identical lifts, all accelerated in the same way at the same instant, so the total force on the shared frame is 7 times that value. Two hold-down clamps then add a further 4 kN and 7 kN to the frame load. What is the total load on the frame, in kN?
w10_P4_003176: A workshop bin holds 254 rivets and another holds 234 clips, and the foreman sorts each bin into equal groups using the largest group size that leaves nothing over in either bin. That group size, as a number, is used as the acceleration in metres per second squared for a test cart of mass 21000 g on a level rail. The engineer finds the force needed to give the cart that acceleration, then subtracts a steady 14 N of drag from it. The remaining force is expressed in kilonewtons, and because 9 carts are run side by side on one frame the figure is multiplied by 9. Finally 1 kN is subtracted to allow for the anchor bracket. The run lasts 45 s. What figure is recorded, in kN?
w10_P4_003183: A robot arm extends so that its reach in metres is 5 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the time. The controller reads how fast that reach is changing at 1.0 s and uses the number it gets as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, that it then commands for a carriage of mass 58000 g. The force that must be applied to the carriage to produce that acceleration is calculated, and a preload of 3 N is added to it. The result is expressed in kilonewtons, and a fixed allowance of 11 kN is then subtracted for the counterweight. The arm draws 3.5 A while it moves. What value is finally reported, in kN?
w10_P4_003184: The figure the test report finally quotes is 4 kJ more than the result of taking 15 kJ away from 6 times the energy described below. Between the 3rd and the 4th second of a run, a shaker table travels at a rate given by 4 times the square of the elapsed time plus 4 times the elapsed time. The total distance the table covers over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is used as the release speed in metres per second of a trolley of mass 18 kg on the rail beside it. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The room is held at 22 degrees Celsius throughout. What figure does the report quote, in kJ?
w10_P4_003186: The number that finally goes in the logbook is 19 kJ less than 9 times the kilojoule reading described next. A store has 88 identical spacers and 72 identical shims, and both are issued in equal-sized packs using the largest pack size that leaves nothing over in either stock. Take that pack size, subtract 6 from it, and use what is left as the release speed in metres per second of a test sled whose mass is 55000 g. The sled runs on a level rail, and the energy it carries because of its motion is measured and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. What number goes in the logbook, in kJ?
w10_P4_003187: The quantity the rig reports at the end is the energy of motion of a flywheel carriage whose mass is 31 kg, in joules. Its release speed in metres per second is built up as follows. A parts store holds 31 brackets and 316 pins, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over from either stock. That batch size has 26 added to it, the result is tripled, and 29 is then taken away, and what remains is the speed in metres per second at which the carriage is released along a level track. The track itself is 18 m long. What does the rig report, in J?
w10_P4_003188: A rail test bench fixes its release setting from a control equation: the setting x must satisfy x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0, and the operator always takes the larger of the two values of x that work. He then adds 23 to that value to obtain the release speed in metres per second of a trolley whose mass is 53 kg. The trolley is released on a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The bench runs 9 trolleys in a single batch, so the batch energy is 9 times that reading, and a full shift consists of 5 identical batches. The trolley body is 0.8 m long. What is the energy for a full shift, in kJ?
w10_P4_003195: A conveyor controller chooses its acceleration setting from the values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0, always taking the larger one, and reads it as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A pallet of mass 177000 g sits on the belt and is accelerated at that rate. The force the belt must apply to the pallet is worked out and a constant 14 N of belt friction is subtracted from it. The remainder is expressed in kilonewtons and multiplied by 9 because 9 conveyor lanes run together on one frame. A final allowance of 14 kN is subtracted for the support frame itself. What figure remains, in kN?
w10_P4_003202: The inspector only ever reads the last line of the day sheet, which is 10 J more than 12 times the value on the line above it. That line above is 5 J less than double the energy figure at the top of the sheet. The energy at the top is the energy carried by a trolley of mass 34000 g because of its motion as it is released along a level bench. Its release speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0. What value does the inspector read, in J?
w10_P4_003207: The last entry in the log is 8 times the entry before it, and that earlier entry is 3 times a figure obtained by taking 16 kJ away from the energy described below. A safety panel has 8 identical switches and any 4 of them may be closed together; the number of different sets of 4 switches that can be chosen is used as the release speed, in metres per second, of a test mass on the rail beside the panel. That test mass weighs 25000 g and runs on a level track. The energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules, and that is the energy the chain above starts from. What is the last entry in the log, in kJ?
w10_P4_003210: On a test bench the charge stored in a coil follows 2 times the cube of the dial setting plus 5 times the square of the dial setting. An engineer measures how fast that stored charge is changing at a dial setting of 2.0, subtracts 9 from the number she gets, and uses the result as the release speed, in metres per second, of a sled of mass 20000 g. The sled is released on a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The bench fires 5 sleds in every cycle and the test consists of 10 identical cycles. The coil itself is rated at 47 ohms. What is the total energy for the whole test, in kJ?
w10_P4_003213: The number the report ends on is 6 times the line before it, and that line is 9 times a figure found by taking 3 kJ off the energy described below. Between the 3rd and the 4th second of a run, a hydraulic ram advances at a rate equal to 2 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that one-second interval, treated as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a carriage whose mass is 35000 g. The carriage runs on a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The ram operates at 180 bar. What number does the report end on, in kJ?
w10_P4_003214: The figure the crane log finally records is the beam load, in kilonewtons, that comes out of the chain below. A hoist controller takes its acceleration setting, in metres per second squared, as the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0. A crate of mass 98 kg is lifted with that acceleration, and the force the cable must apply to the crate is calculated. A preload of 10 N is added to that force, the result is doubled because a second identical cable shares the same beam, and it is doubled again when a matching pair of beams is installed. What does the crane log record, in kN?
w10_P4_003215: A control panel has 8 identical relays, and exactly 4 of them are closed in any given configuration; the number of different configurations available is used as the acceleration setting, in metres per second squared, for a shuttle of mass 18 kg. The force the drive must apply to the shuttle to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. An allowance of 9 kN is then subtracted for the guide rail. The remainder is multiplied by 5 because 5 identical shuttles share one drive frame. Finally 29 kN of static frame preload is added. What is the resulting frame load, in kN?
w10_P4_003218: The number at the end of the sheet is 7 times the line above it, and that line is 12 times the kilonewton figure worked out below. A cam profile gives the follower displacement as 2 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 1 times the square of the shaft angle. How fast that displacement is changing at a shaft angle of 3.0 is taken as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a slide whose mass is 139000 g. The force needed to accelerate the slide at that rate is found, 17 N of friction is subtracted from it, and the remainder is expressed in kilonewtons to give that figure. The shaft turns at 250 rpm. What number is at the end of the sheet, in kN?
w10_P4_003219: The figure the rig displays at the end is 14 kN more than a value that is itself 21 kN more than 3 times the kilonewton reading described below. A drive cam gives the follower position as 3 times the cube of the input angle plus 4 times the square of the input angle. The rate at which that position is changing at an input angle of 2.0 is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a carriage whose mass is 100 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage to accelerate it that hard is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons to give that reading. The carriage rides on rails 6 m apart. What figure does the rig display, in kN?
w10_P4_003221: An automated press sets its acceleration from the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0, and then adds 25 to that value, reading the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. The ram it drives has a mass of 137000 g. The controller works out the force needed to accelerate the ram at that rate. Because 6 presses on the line fire together, the total force carried by the shared floor beam is 6 times that force. The line runs at 40 strokes per minute. What is the total force on the beam, in kN?
w10_P4_003225: During the first stage of a launch, from the 2nd to the 4th second, a catapult arm moves at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total travel of the arm over that interval, taken as a plain number, is used as the acceleration in metres per second squared applied to a payload of mass 108 kg. The force that must act on the payload to accelerate it at that rate is calculated. The catapult has 5 identical arms pulling on one yoke, and 2 such yokes feed a single anchor. A static preload of 23 N is then added at the anchor. What is the total force at the anchor, in N?
w10_P4_003230: The value stamped on the test certificate is the frame force in kilonewtons that comes out of the chain below. A test rig moves a probe so that its displacement is 4 times the cube of the elapsed time minus 4 times the square of the elapsed time. How fast that displacement is changing at 1.0 s is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a carriage of mass 53 kg. The force needed to accelerate the carriage at that rate is calculated, then multiplied by 10 because 10 identical carriages are driven from one frame, and a fixed 23 N of preload is added to the frame total. The frame is 4.5 m wide. What is stamped on the certificate, in kN?
w10_P4_003231: A baggage conveyor takes its acceleration setting, in metres per second squared, as the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. A case of mass 26 kg is accelerated at that rate by the belt. The force the belt must apply to the case is worked out, and since 10 identical cases sit on the belt at once the belt load is 10 times that force. That load is expressed in kilonewtons. A steady 21 kN of tension from the drive drum is then added to it. The terminal handles 900 bags per hour. What is the total tension in the belt, in kN?
w10_P4_003234: The number the control log records is 24 N less than the drive force described below. During a pour, a ladle tips at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total tilt accumulated from the 0th to the 3rd second, taken as a plain number, has 3 subtracted from it, the remainder is multiplied by 3, and 8 is then added, and the result is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a transfer carriage of mass 106 kg. The drive force in question is the force that must be applied to that carriage to accelerate it at that rate. What number does the control log record, in N?
w10_P4_003238: The last number on the commissioning sheet is 19 kN more than the kilonewton figure worked out below. A press controller adds its two calibration constants 7 and 13, multiplies the sum by 2, and then subtracts 4, treating the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A tool head of mass 147 kg is accelerated at that rate, and the force the drive must apply to it is calculated. Because 4 identical tool heads are driven from one frame, the frame carries 4 times that force, and the frame load is then expressed in kilonewtons. The press stands 3.2 m tall. What is the last number on the commissioning sheet, in kN?
